title: A mask for solver messages before they reach a log

blocks.text: A warehouse-planning service forwards solver messages to a shared log. Some messages name the machine's user and host, or carry an e-mail address or an access key, and none of that may reach the log. Write `mask_line(line)`, which returns the line with:

rows: `user ` followed by any characters up to the next `,` or `)` (possibly none)
`host ` followed by any characters up to the next `,` or `)` (possibly none)
an e-mail address: name characters (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `+`, `-`), `@`, then a domain with at least one dot
a key shaped like a UUID: 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12 hexadecimal digits joined by `-`

blocks.text: Everything else stays as it was, so the message still says what went wrong. "user" and "host" count only as whole words (`hostid` is not `host`). Python's `re` module does all of it. No Gurobi license is needed. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import re

RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"\buser [^,)]*"), "user <user>"),
    (re.compile(r"\bhost [^,)]*"), "host <host>"),
    (re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(\.[\w-]+)+"), "<email>"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}\b"), "<key>"),
]


def mask_line(line: str) -> str:
    """The line with users, hosts, e-mail addresses and UUID-shaped keys replaced by placeholders."""
    for pattern, placeholder in RULES:
        line = pattern.sub(placeholder, line)
    return line


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(mask_line("No license found (user dock, host rack-9) for ops@example.com"))

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from masking import mask_line

# Made-up solver messages.
messages = [
    "No license found (user pat, host bench-3, cores 4)",
    "License issued to jane.doe@example.invalid until May",
    "key 0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d expired",
    "Model has 812 rows and 1,040 columns",
]
for message in messages:
    print(f"{message!r} ->", mask_line(message))

cases.says: the values after 'user ' and 'host ' become <user> and <host>, the rest of the line kept
a line with no user, host, address or key comes back as it was
'user , host box1' masks the empty user and the host
an e-mail address anywhere in the line becomes <email>
a UUID-shaped key such as a WLS access id becomes <key>
